effects: Pulls `shares` vault shares (krfUSDC) from the signer into the withdrawal queue with transferFrom. This spends the signer's allowance on the vault token.
Mints a new withdrawal NFT to `receiver`. Whoever holds this NFT is the only one who can claim the underlying assets later.
Calls sweepPending on the vault's delegator. This does not touch the signer's assets.
There is no cancel function, so the queued shares cannot be taken back. They can only be claimed as assets once the queue is filled.
formats.shown: Queue X krfUSDC shares from the vault, NFT goes to the receiver. Fields show the vault address, the share amount with its token and the NFT recipient.

findings.title: requestRedeem: 'NFT to {receiver}' does not say the receiver gets the right to claim the assets.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol requestRedeem: `_mint(receiver, tokenId)`; claim: `if (ownerOf(tokenId) != msg.sender) revert NotTokenOwner();`. Descriptor interpolatedIntent "Queue {shares}, NFT to {receiver}" and label 'NFT recipient'. In cases 0 and 2 the receiver is a third party, so the signer gives away the claim, and the screen calls it only 'NFT'.
findings.fix: Use wording like 'Queue {shares} for withdrawal; claim rights (NFT) go to {receiver}' and label the field 'Withdrawal claim owner'.

findings.title: requestRedeem: the screen gives no expected underlying amount, and the request is irreversible.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol: assets are fixed at fill() time via `IERC4626(vault).redeem(...)`. No cancel function exists. The descriptor shows only the share amount.
findings.fix: Optionally add to the intent that the request cannot be cancelled. The asset amount cannot come from calldata.

findings.title: requestRedeem: the Vault field and the share token come from a hardcoded constant, not from the queue's `vault` storage.
findings.evidence: descriptor metadata.constants.vault = 0x007e0B8E99c6134E81A1eAAE754460E3202cB671, used as `params.token`. In WithdrawalQueue.sol the token pulled is `IERC20(vault)`, a storage variable set in _initialize. This holds only while the constant matches.
findings.fix: None needed if the constant is the queue's vault. Keep it pinned to this single deployment.

effects: Requires the signer to own withdrawal NFT `tokenId`.
Sends the vault's underlying asset (`IERC4626(vault).asset()`, e.g. USDC) to `receiver`. The amount is whatever part of the request has been filled and not yet claimed, and may be zero or partial.
Marks those shares as claimed. The NFT stays with the signer and is not burned.
formats.shown: Claim filled withdrawal #tokenId to the receiver. Fields show the vault address, the NFT ID and the asset recipient.

findings.title: claim: the screen never names the asset that is paid out.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claim: `IERC20(IERC4626(vault).asset()).safeTransfer(receiver, assets);`. The descriptor's intent "Claim filled withdrawal" and field 'Asset recipient' do not name the asset (the vault's underlying, USDC for krfUSDC).
findings.fix: Name the underlying asset in the intent or a label, e.g. 'Claim USDC from withdrawal {tokenId} to {receiver}'.

findings.title: claim: the amount paid depends on the fill state, not on calldata, so it cannot be shown.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claim: `(assets, shares) = claimable(tokenId);`. The amount is computed from the _cumulSharesToCumulAssets checkpoints and can be partial or zero.
findings.fix: No descriptor fix. Optionally say 'claims the filled portion' so users expect a partial amount.

findings.title: claim: 'Claim filled withdrawal' suggests a full payout, but a partial claim is possible and the NFT stays with the signer.
findings.evidence: WithdrawalQueue.sol claimable: `endShares = Math.min(request.prevRequestSum + request.shares, totalFilled())`. claim does not burn the NFT. Case 3 description: 'sends assets, retains NFT'.
findings.fix: Use wording like 'Claim available (filled) portion of withdrawal {tokenId}'.

findings.title: claim: the withdrawal NFT ID is shown raw, with no link to the queue NFT collection.
findings.fix: Use format nftName with collection set to the queue contract (@.to).

claim(uint256 tokenId,address receiver).worst: claim: the screen never names the asset that is paid out.
